name: Kamasa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only source: Lloyd 1973 'The Angan language family' (in Franklin ed., PL C-26) — family survey/classification cited by Glottolog; no grammar or phonology of Kamasa exists; archive.org has only a Swadesh list.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1973. Appendices (Appendix A.6 Kamasa, p. 548). In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 539-592. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Swadesh-100 Kamasa word list (99 forms, apostrophe = glottal stop, verb stems underlined); page scan checked: no stress, pitch or tone marks on any form; appendix introduction (p. 541) has no transcription note on suprasegmentals.
sources.venue: The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. 2010. Kamasa Swadesh List. Internet Archive item rosettaproject_klp_swadesh-1 (CC BY 3.0; source not stated, forms match Lloyd 1973:548).
sources.note: Word list only; one form 'boipuyá' carries an acute that corresponds to the glottal-stop apostrophe of Lloyd's boipu'ya (item 50), not a stress mark. No stress information.

sources.citation: Smith, Geoffrey P. 1988. Morobe counting systems. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26, 1-132. Pacific Linguistics A-76. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 90 KAMASA: 'No field data were collected, but the following numbers were taken from word lists prepared by Lloyd (1973:548). 1 hunaninko 2 hukwego.' Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kama1360 and reference pages 140544 (Lloyd 1973) and 319180 (Fischer 1968).
sources.note: Nearly extinct; 0 descriptive (grammar/sketch/phonology) references; Lloyd 1973 tagged overview;comparative;phonology for 11 Angan languages incl. Kamasa. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lloyd, Richard G. 1973. The Angan language family. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 31-110. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C26.31
sources.note: Sec. 2.10 Kamasa (pp. 77-79) is the only description: a one-page phonology outline from survey word lists (12 consonants, 7 vowels, voicing after nasals, voiceless final vowels, 'phonemic system appears to be like Ampale'); nothing on stress, tone, pitch or accent for Kamasa. Family-level only, p. 87: 'Tone and stress are combined in a complex unit which usually occurs in connection with the grammatical stem.. Angaataha is like a tone language and the others are more intonation languages'; p. 95: Angan languages 'have complex supra-segmental systems, usually a combination of pitch and stress'…
sources.venue: The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea

sources.citation: SIL-PNG survey/word-list materials on Kamasa (Lloyd & West SIL survey word list, cited Lloyd 1973:107; source of Ethnologue's 2003 count of 7 speakers) -- OLAC klp listing and SIL PNG language page could not be reached by automated download
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: OLAC/SIL listings are the only place an unpublished phonology note or later survey report on Kamasa would surface; the 2003 speaker figure implies a post-1973 SIL visit whose report was not located.

sources.note: Glottolog-listed wordlist that may re-transcribe the Kamasa list; word lists only, so at most stress marks, not a statement.

sources.citation: Fischer, Hans. 1968. Negwa: Eine Papua-Gruppe im Wandel. München: Klaus Renner. 493 pp. (Kamasa = Inetje/Kwamogh; 16-word table p. 33; Yagwoia phonology notes pp. 21-22)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only other primary source with Kamasa data; Lloyd 1973 (p. 96) hoped Fischer's 'work on Kawacha and Kamasa will soon become available'. Per Lloyd's summary it holds only a few Kamasa words and no Kamasa phonology, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the sole unchecked item.

sources.citation: Fischer, Hans. 1968. Kurze Wörterliste einiger Kuku-Kuku-Dialekte. In Negwa: Eine Papua-Gruppe im Wandel, p. 33. München: Klaus Renner (493 pp).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Glottolog record: a 16-word comparative table (p. 33) including Kamasa (Fischer's Kwamogh/Inetje). Lloyd 1973 Appendix G (pp. 103-104), which summarises the book, says Fischer 'recorded only a few words in the Angaataha, Kamasa and Menya languages' and that his phonology notes (pp. 21-22) concern Yagwoia only. No scan located (Open Library record only).
